angle: AI attacks move at machine speed; your security operating model needs to as well.
sourceTitle: The speed problem: How frontier AI exposes weakness in enterprise cybersecurity
linkedinPost:
Your security team moves in weeks. Attackers move in seconds.

A McKinsey piece nails it: frontier AI has shifted cyber from a tooling race to an operating-model problem. Offense is automated and fast; defense is committee-based and slow.

What closes the gap isn’t another dashboard. It’s decision rights, pre-approved playbooks, and automation wired into incident response.

From the FDE trenches, the companies that hold the line do five things:
- Codify “if X, then Y” playbooks with legal/comms sign-off in advance.
- Push decisions down: on-call leads can isolate, revoke, or roll keys without a meeting.
- Automate first response (detect, contain, rotate) and review after.
- Run red-team drills at machine speed—measure time-to-contain, not slideware readiness.
- Stand up an exec war-room cadence that can ship policy changes in days, not quarters.

If your MTTR and key-rotation times still depend on calendars instead of code, you’re not ready for AI-era threats.

Where does your current operating model slow you down most—policy, people, or plumbing? #EnterpriseAI #AIStrategy #AITransformation
